elements.content: Grammar focus: Cleft Sentences for Emphasis.

Core Rule: It-Cleft: It + Be + Highlighted Element + That/Who + Rest of Sentence . Wh-Cleft: What / All + Clause + Be + Highlighted Element .

It-Cleft (Subject) — It is/was + Subject + that/who...: It was the financial director who identified the accounting discrepancy.
It-Cleft (Adverbial) — It is/was + Adverbial + that...: It was only after the audit that structural vulnerabilities emerged.
Wh-Cleft (Pseudo-cleft) — What + S + V + is/was + Clause: What concerns the board most is long-term fiscal sustainability.
Guided practice: choose the correct option.
1. Which sentence is a correctly formed It-cleft?
options: It was the lack of oversight that led to the crisis.
What led to the crisis it was the lack of oversight.

elements.content: 2. What element follows 'What + clause + is/was' in a Wh-cleft?
Read and listen: three examples in context.

What surprised me was her calm.
It was in 2019 that we met.
All he did was smile.
The thing I like most is silence.
1. Which sentence is a correctly formed It-cleft?
options: It was the lack of oversight that led to the crisis.
What led to the crisis it was the lack of oversight.
